**Syncom Formulations (SYNCOMF): 40/100, AVOID for now**
- The numbers fit the pattern well:
  - Six-quarter OPM climb, 12% to 22%.
  - Debt down from 83 to about 0.
  - FII 0.35% to 2.23%.
  - Recomputed P/E 21.7x.
- But no operational cause could be found. There is no new plant. The only cited 2026 capital spend is a ₹57 cr purchase of commercial property in Andheri, a capital-allocation flag.
- Other income is about 27% of PBT. The base is about 4.2 lakh retail holders on a ₹22 stock, and the CFO changed in August 2026.
- Per the skill rule, a margin jump with no identifiable cause is a reason to downgrade.

body:
- **FPI outflows:**
  - FPIs pulled about ₹2.45 lakh crore out of Indian equities by the third week of Sept 2026, against a record ₹1.66 lakh crore in 2025. PL Capital puts 2025 at about ₹1.7 lakh crore.
  - Sources: [Ziromarket](https://www.ziromarket.com/blog/fpi-outflows-india-2026-record); [PL India](https://www.plindia.com/news/foreign-funds-flee-fii-outflows-in-five-months-of-2026-already-exceed-full-year-2025-total/)
- **SEBI bulletin (Apr 2026):**
  - FPIs were net sellers of ₹1,25,736 crore across asset classes in FY26, with the steepest monthly sell-off in March 2026.
  - Cumulative net DII inflow was a record ₹8.5 lakh crore in FY26, tied to record SIP flows.
  - Source: [SEBI Bulletin](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/apr-2026/1777539656528.pdf)
- **DII offset in 2026:** DIIs bought ₹4.16 lakh crore in 2026 against ₹2.7 lakh crore of FII selling. — [Kalkine](https://www.kalkine.co.in/article/investment/domestic-institutions-offset-rs-27-lakh-crore-of-fii-selling-as-sip-inflows-stay-robust-in-2026)
- **SIP figures:**
  - Ziromarket reports ₹32,297 crore in Aug 2026.
  - Kalkine reports ₹32,087 crore in Mar 2026 and ₹31,115 crore in Apr 2026.
  - Monumoney cites ₹26,632 crore, which conflicts. Verify against AMFI.
  - Sources: [Ziromarket](https://www.ziromarket.com/blog/fpi-outflows-india-2026-record); [Kalkine](https://www.kalkine.co.in/article/investment/domestic-institutions-offset-rs-27-lakh-crore-of-fii-selling-as-sip-inflows-stay-robust-in-2026); [Monumoney](https://monumoney.in/blog/sip-record-26632-cr-fpi-outflow-2026-exit-liquidity)
- **MSCI weight:** India's MSCI EM weight fell from about 20% (Sep 2024) to 11.94% (30 Apr 2026). Passive funds must follow. — [Finnovate](https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/msci-em-india-weight-fpi-flows-taiwan-korea); [Multibagg](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/india-fii-flows-em-valuation-cmqbsct4l01rks60joxx6bf8i)
- **Valuation premium:** India's forward P/E premium over MSCI EM was cited at about 77% at the peak. Other sources say the premium compressed to about a two-decade low by 2026, so sources conflict on timing. — [Multibagg](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/fii-selling-india-2026-outflows-cmpk1hw2fp4cgr20jzh8nlp03); [Investace](https://investacecapital.com/research/fii/)
- **Sector selling:** BFSI led FPI selling, with about $18bn out in 45 days around Mar–Apr 2026. In May 2026 the outflow was $3.44bn. — [Finnovate Apr](https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/fpi-selling-india-half-april-2026-bfsi-sectoral-flows); [Finnovate May](https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/fpi-flows-may-2026-india-sectoral-analysis)
- **Partial reversal:** FPIs added ₹23,544 crore in Aug 2026, attributed to earnings and rupee stability. — [Multibagg](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/fii-fpi-india-2026-flows-cmoihcj2us18tp30j229mjvsc)
- **Earnings and the rupee:** Nifty quarterly profit growth was cited at 12.9% and the forward P/E at about 17.6. The rupee was near 96.78 per USD in Oct 2026. — [Multibagg](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/india-fii-flows-em-valuation-cmqbsct4l01rks60joxx6bf8i); [Dezerv](https://www.dezerv.in/blog/indian-equities-in-2026-is-the-earnings-cycle-turning/)

body: **Summary:** Alcobev companies make and brand spirits, beer and wine. Price is regulated state by state, and excise duties are often 60–80% of the consumer price. Profit comes from premiumisation (Prestige and Above spirits carry far higher margins than regular brands), gross margin over ENA/grain and glass, and A&P efficiency. Each state is effectively its own market with its own route to market (government corporations or private retail), price approvals and duty changes. Key metrics: volume by segment (P&A against regular), premium share of revenue, gross margin, EBITDA margin, A&P %, price increases secured from states, ENA/grain and glass costs, state concentration, and net debt (Radico's deleveraging). Cycle drivers: state excise policy (the Maharashtra 50–60% duty hike of June 2025 and MML policy; Karnataka; Andhra and Telangana route-to-market changes), grain and ENA prices (FCI rice for ethanol diverts supply), glass prices, consumer premiumisation, the India–UK FTA cutting Scotch duty, and weather for beer. Lead indicators: state excise revenue data, ISWAI commentary, maize/grain prices, CIABC releases, company P&A volume disclosures. Winners (Radico 2016–26 on premium mix and deleveraging; United Spirits after its Diageo clean-up, shedding popular brands) leaned into premiumisation, got state pricing approvals and avoided governance issues. Losers took state bans (Bihar 2016) or were stuck in regular-brand price wars and beer cost spikes. Valuation: P/E 50–90x for spirits leaders. Radico re-rated from ~18x to ~90x. Nov 2026: Radico Q2 FY27 P&A volume grew 36% to 5.28 mn cases (FY27 target raised to 30%) while total IMFL rose only 7%. United Spirits NSV grew only +2.8% on Maharashtra/Karnataka headwinds. Traps: a state policy shock, and paying 80x for premium growth. Sources: [1](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/radico-fy27-premium-growth-target-concall-cmw1fmdww009u31qltk2uc0ay) · [2](https://www.investywise.com/?p=124785) · [3](https://www.exchange4media.com/marketing-news/premium-pours-popular-spirits-falter-is-indias-alcobev-market-looking-at-a-divide-160107.html) · [4](https://www.zeebiz.com/india/news-maharashtra-cabinet-approves-up-to-60-liquor-duty-hike-united-spirits-radico-allied-blenders-stocks-under-pressure-368784) Links: about `case_study:radico-khaitan`

body:
**False alarm: Netflix's -$3.3 bn free cash flow** (`case_study:false-alarm-netflix-negative-fcf`, verified). FLAG: free cash flow negative for years, about -$3.0 bn (2018) and -$3.27 bn (2019, 10-K), funded by junk bonds; cash content spending ~$14.6 bn vs only ~$9.2 bn of content amortisation in 2019, so reported profit overstated cash generation. Short sellers called it a debt-funded content treadmill. CONTEXT: (1) original content is a capital asset that builds a library and global brand; the gap between cash spend and amortisation was the growth investment; (2) subscribers and engagement grew globally with low churn, and prices could be raised; (3) content spend is a fixed cost spread over a growing base, so margins would rise with scale. FCF turned positive in 2020 (COVID production pause helped) and became large later as operating margin rose toward ~30% [post-2020 FCF levels from memory, unverified]. The stock still crashed -76% in 2021-22 on the first subscriber loss. LESSON: negative FCF is benign when the spend creates a durable asset that scales over a growing, retained customer base and the cash gap shrinks as a share of revenue; it is dangerous when the spend must rise faster than revenue just to stand still.

**False alarm (on survival), real (on valuation): Tesla's losses and $12 bn of share sales** (`case_study:false-alarm-tesla-losses-dilution`, verified). FLAGS: GAAP losses every year until 2020; repeated equity raises; in 2020 alone $2 bn (Feb), $5 bn at-the-market (Sep) and $5 bn at-the-market (Dec) = $12 bn; extreme short interest; P/E >100 at the 2021 peak. CONTEXT: by mid-2019 the Model 3 ramp (~5k/week), a surprise Q3-2019 profit and the Shanghai factory built in ~10 months showed the survival risk was ending. The 2020 share sales were made after a ~650% rally at a ~$500 bn valuation, so each $5 bn was only ~1% dilution: cheap capital that fully funded new factories (Giga Texas) and removed bankruptcy risk. Dilution at a high price, for growth capex, is a gift to existing holders; dilution at a low price to survive is a transfer from them. Stock: ~$11.8 split-adjusted (Jun 2019) -> ~$414 (Nov 2021), ~35x. WHERE THE FLAG CAME TRUE: the price was mostly rerating; it fell -73% to ~$101 (Jan 2023) when auto margins fell. LESSON: measure dilution as % of shares and ask the price and purpose; separate 'will it survive?' from 'is it worth this price?'.

- **Citation counts** come from Semantic Scholar (S2) or Crossref (CR), fetched 2026-11-20/21. Both run well below Google Scholar, often by 2-4x, so read them as relative weight, not absolute counts. OpenAlex was unavailable because the shared IP's daily budget was used up. S2 search was heavily rate-limited, so some counts come from DOI lookups.
- **Effect sizes** come from abstracts, open-access PDFs (the IIMA working paper and the Marisetty-Subrahmanyam NYU archive copy) and well-known published figures. Records whose numbers rest on one paper or summary are marked `single-source`.
